Enum Class Rank

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Enum<Rank>
np.cincuentazo.model.Rank
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Comparable<Rank>, Constable
public enum Rank extends Enum<Rank>
Represents the thirteen ranks of a standard poker deck, each carrying the scoring logic defined by the Cincuentazo rules.

Value rules

  • 2â€“8, 10 â†’ add their face number to the table sum.
  • 9 â†’ neutral; neither adds nor subtracts (value = 0).
  • J, Q, K â†’ subtract 10 from the table sum (value = -10).
  • A â†’ adds 1 or 10, whichever keeps the sum â‰¤ 50. This decision requires the current table sum, so the Ace's final value is resolved in Card.getValue(int) rather than here. getBaseValue() returns ACE_FLEXIBLE as a sentinel for that case.

Why put value logic in the enum?

The value of a card depends exclusively on its rank â€” not on which specific card object is in play. Encoding it here avoids scattering switch or if-else chains across the codebase and makes it trivial to unit-test every rank in isolation.

    • getBaseValue

      public int getBaseValue()
      Returns the base scoring value for this rank.

      Important: for ACE, this method returns ACE_FLEXIBLE. Callers must not use that value in arithmetic; they must call Card.getValue(int) instead to obtain the context-aware value (1 or 10).

      Returns:
      the scoring delta this rank applies to the table sum, or ACE_FLEXIBLE if the rank is ACE
